name: Jude Wick
life: Jude built wheels for speed until a neighborhood kid asked for one that could survive falling over every day. He has had a box of mismatched practice spokes by the counter ever since. On Saturday, near Juniper Street, Jude knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: Both wheels were built in my shop. I spoke for the wheel I remembered, and the child corrected me. I keep her drawing of the spoke pattern over the truing stand.
appearance: Jude is easy to recognize by a blunt cut just below the ears and full cheeks and a mouth that pulls slightly to one side. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand, Jude looks down for a moment before saying something difficult when listening.
personality: Jude is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To give the child credit for identifying the wheel.
family: Samuel Mehta is Jude’s half-sibling. Jude leaves the first voice message. Samuel calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The last light at the harbor*, Samuel says, “I turn ours off from below because my hands no longer reach the switch.”
connections: Opal Finch. They trust the child's description after the bell and the spokes offer two independent ways to identify the bike.

reactions.situation: A child's account contradicts the adult at the counter
reactions.response: Jude lets the child finish describing the bicycle and asks to hear the bell.
